questions.question: A feature has mean 10 and standard deviation 2. What is the z-score of x=16?
For Q1=10 and Q3=14, the IQR is 4. Which value is above the usual upper fence Q3+1.5*IQR?
questions.explanation: The upper fence is 14+1.5(4)=20. A value of 22 is beyond it.

questions.question: Fifty login failures in a row are normal individually but unusual as a sequence. What kind of anomaly is this?
questions.explanation: The unusual behavior comes from the group or temporal pattern, so it is collective rather than a single isolated point.

questions.question: How does an Isolation Forest tend to identify an outlier?
options: It has the largest class label in a supervised training set
It is isolated by random splits in fewer steps than typical points
It is always the point with the highest z-score on feature one
It receives a probability of exactly one from every tree
questions.explanation: Anomalies are often easier to separate, giving them shorter average path lengths in the random partition trees.

questions.question: An unsupervised detector flags many novel events but also many legitimate ones. Which tradeoff is being exposed?
options: Recall and precision must always rise together
The detector has become a supervised classifier
Higher anomaly coverage can come with lower precision
A larger feature matrix guarantees fewer false positives
questions.explanation: A broad detector may catch more unknown anomalies while producing more false alarms; the operating threshold must reflect the response cost.

questions.question: When fitting an unsupervised detector for a stable service, which training data are safest?
options: Only the most extreme alerts from last month
A mixture of future incidents and normal rows with no time split
The labels of a different classification task
A period believed to contain normal behavior
questions.explanation: Modeling a clean normal baseline makes unusual observations stand out; contaminating it with many anomalies shifts that baseline.
